newsitem.title: USA: Lucent wins contract from Indonesia's Telkom.
newsitem.headline: Lucent wins contract from Indonesia's Telkom.

text.p: The head of Indonesia's national domestic telecommunications company PT Telkom said on Thursday Lucent Technologies Inc had won a $22.7 million equipment contract from Telkom.
Telkom chief executive A.A. Nasution told reporters the contract was part of the company's goal "to be seen as a world-class operation by ... the year 2001."
The equipment will allow state-owned Telkom to expand its data communications network and improve its services to business customers.
A Lucent spokesman also said the company and AT&T Corp would train some Telkom managers and technicians. The training agreement was drawn up with AT&T, which is spinning off Lucent.
Nasution met analysts in New York and also in Japan, Singapore, Hong Kong and London to update financial markets about Telkom. He said no deals were planned to be signed.

Nasution said there were no plans to seek a strategic partnership with a foreign company, saying Telkom was guaranteed exclusivity for domestic service for the next 15 years and for international calls through 2005.
The number of employees has been set at 37,350 and there were no plans to lay off workers. Nasution said 150 workers who retired this year would be replaced.
Finance director Harry Supangkat said Telkom foresaw capital spending of about 4.8 trillion rupiats ($2.06 billion) this year and 4.2 trillion ($1.8 billion) next year.
He said the drop would come as the company used up revenues from its initial public offering of 20 percent of its stock completed in November 1995.
Instead of issuing more stock or taking on more debt, "we try to cover all these needs from our own resources, because investors will not be happy if we have a lot of debt," he said.
